summary.headline: Coforge raised FY27 consolidated EBIT margin guidance to 16% from 15.5% and signed a record eight large deals, with order intake above $1 billion.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was $652.2 million, up 10.9% sequentially in constant currency, with organic sequential growth of 3.8% CC. Consolidated EBIT margin came in at 16%, ahead of the 15.5% guidance, and management raised the FY27 target to 16% and guided to a 17% reported Q4 EBIT. Order intake exceeded $1 billion (up 51% QoQ) and the next-12-month executable order book hit a record $2.4 billion, up 45% YoY. The first full quarter of the Encore (In Core) integration showed flat revenue of roughly $147-148 million on an organic basis, with management saying Encore growth will mirror Coforge from Q3.

financial_highlights.change: 10.1% QoQ in USD, 10.9% QoQ in CC, 11.6% QoQ in INR
Ahead of 15.5% FY27 guidance; H1 EBIT margin 20.5%
Acquisition-related guidance of $15-16 million overrun to about $17 million
Expected $7.1 million MTM loss in Q3 and $1.2 million in Q4

segments.commentary: Americas grew 4.1% and Rest of World grew 16.3% QoQ organically. Order intake: $455m North America, $485m Europe, $101m RoW.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBIT margin raised to 16% from 15.5%; H1 at 20.5% and management reiterated the 20.5-21% range for the full year.
Reported Q4 FY27 EBIT margin targeted at 17%, with margins expected to stay above 17% thereafter and a further significant expansion in FY28 (exit margin to carry into next year).
FY27 FCF to PAT guidance of 100% maintained; management expects to exceed 100% by year end.
Steady-state tax rate of 23-24%; no exceptional items expected in Q3 onward; hedge losses to fall to $7.1m in Q3 and $1.2m in Q4.
Encore revenue growth to mirror Coforge growth from Q3 FY27; management expressed equal confidence for FY28.
Management aims to be among the top three highest-EBIT-margin tech services firms in the short to medium term and expects to be the industry growth leader for a third consecutive year.
capex_capacity: Utilization at 82.4% versus peers at 86%+, cited as a significant margin lever.
Forward-deployed engineer (Momentum Blue) factory being built on site; heavy ongoing investment expected to cause a material gross margin spike from Q4 at consolidated level.
Near-shore capability built across Eastern Europe and Latin America via Encore acquisition.
AI in production: 520+ AI engagements for 225+ clients with 260+ agents deployed in live operations.
demand_pricing: Eight large deals signed in Q2, the highest in company history; management targets eight or more in Q3 (the shortest quarter).
Top 5 clients were 18.1% of Q2 revenue, top 10 were 26.4%; top 10 and top 20 accounts are both growing 20%+ YoY.
Second client has crossed a $100 million annualized run-rate; management says this client is among the highest-margin accounts.
Management says most deals are proactive, sole-sourced deals rather than procurement-driven RFPs, to avoid price competition; management also cited growing deal flow via advisory channels.
AI-led services (AI, engineering, data, integration, cloud) contributed 86% of consolidated revenue in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Are the margin gains from AI sustainable, and are new AI deals coming at better pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current margin uptake is coming from existing fixed-price projects where AI is being infused, not from newly priced deals. Benefits are expected to show in Q4. Some efficiencies are passed to clients, but management says net margin is positive.

qa_highlights.question: Can Coforge sustain growth by relying only on sole-sourced deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it intends to accelerate growth, attributing the industry slowdown to fewer procurement-driven RFPs, and expects advisory-channel deals to add to the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin gains from GNA optimization be reinvested in SG&A and growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SG&A has not been cut; revenue grew 53% YoY while GNA grew 15.6%. It said growth remains the first priority and that it will invest to sustain it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow conversion fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to legal entity rationalization and tax restructuring, which delayed contract transfers from US to India and caused invoicing and collection delays, raising unbilled revenue. It expects this to correct.

qa_highlights.question: How is Encore's revenue trending and how is the order book split?
qa_highlights.answer: Encore revenue was flat QoQ at about $147-148 million on an organic basis. The largest pipeline deal and largest healthcare client both come from Encore. Deal intake and order book now include Encore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EPS and hedge-loss outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exceptional items go to zero and hedge losses fall sharply, which together with margin expansion should lift Q4 EPS; an analyst estimated Rs 19-20. Minority interest stays flat because it relates to a JV in which the client holds 20%.

risks_watch: Acute pricing pressure in the industry and AI-led deflation; management acknowledges some efficiency is passed to clients.
Q4 margin of 17% depends on fixed-price AI efficiencies and GNA levers; the gross margin investment in Momentum Blue could weigh before benefits show.
Encore revenue was flat QoQ in Q2; management says growth will match Coforge from Q3, so Q3 Encore organic growth is a key test.
Healthcare and High Tech declined 6.4% QoQ; watch recovery in these verticals.
Working capital and FCF to PAT conversion (89% in Q2) needs to reach 100% by year end; the rise in unbilled revenue is a monitoring item.
Acquisition exceptional costs overran to about $17 million against the $15-16 million guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat throughout, with management repeatedly stating a "critical tipping point" for AI adoption and an intent to lead the industry on growth and margin. Answers on Encore integration and deal momentum were firm, while answers on the source of margin gains were more general and emphasised future outcomes rather than current data.
key_quotes: We are pleased to raise our consolidated EBIT margin guidance for fiscal year 27 to 16 percent from the 15.5 percent we had shared at the beginning of the year.
In quarter two, we signed eight large deals. This is the highest number of large deals we have signed in any quarter in our history.
Growth is the first, second and the third imperative as far as we are concerned we will not let anything come in the way of it.
We remain confident of delivering FCEF to PAD guidance of 100% for F527.

growth.why: Management raised FY27 EBIT margin guide to 16% (from 15.5%) and guided 17% for Q4, backed by a record $2.4B executable order book (+45% YoY) and over $1B order intake, but revenue growth guidance is not quantified and margin gains rely on cost and utilisation levers rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBIT margin 16% in Q2 vs 15.5% guide; H1 at 20.5%, Q4 targeted at 17% and management flags a significant further expansion in FY28, with utilisation at 82.4% vs peers 86%+ as a lever.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Momentum Blue forward-deployed engineer factory is under construction on site and Encore near-shore capability (Eastern Europe, LatAm) is already commissioned, but no new delivery capacity sized or dated in the brief.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Next-12-month executable order book at a record $2.4B (+45% YoY) and order intake above $1B (+51% QoQ) with eight large deals signed and eight or more targeted in Q3; Q2 organic CC growth was 3.8% sequentially.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 82.4%, which is high, but the brief shows no board-level capex plan; the Momentum Blue factory is already under way and the stated margin lever is utilisation, not new plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 consolidated EBIT margin was raised to 16% from 15.5% and Q2 landed ahead of guide, but revenue guidance is not quantified and the Q4 17% target depends on fixed-price AI efficiencies not yet visible in data.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 margin depends on AI efficiencies and GNA levers; Momentum Blue gross margin investment could weigh before benefits show, Encore was flat QoQ at about $147-148M, and FCF to PAT (89% in Q2) must reach 100%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launches were discussed; AI agent deployments (260+ agents live) are already in production.

rows.label: Encore revenue to mirror Coforge growth from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Encore revenue was flat QoQ at about $147-148M organic in Q2; management says growth matches Coforge from Q3, so Q3 organic growth is the key test.

rows.label: Exceptional items roll off from Q3
rows.why: Q2 exceptional items were $5.9M and the acquisition cost overran to about $17M; management says no exceptionals from Q3, and hedge losses fall to $7.1M in Q3 and $1.2M in Q4.

rows.label: FCF to PAT reaches 100% by year end
rows.why: FCF to PAT was 89% in Q2 and 92% in H1, with unbilled revenue rising from contract transfer delays; management holds 100% guidance and expects to exceed it by year end.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin trajectory, record order book and Encore integration, but answers on the source of margin gains and sustaining growth without procurement-driven RFPs stayed general; analysts' Q&A focus was on AI pricing, GNA reinvestment and cash conversion.

oneOffs.what: Encore (In Core) consolidation contributes to reported QoQ growth; Encore revenue flat at about $147-148m organically in Q2, so the 10.9% CC QoQ headline includes acquired-business effects
$5.9m exceptional items in Q2 (acquisition-related), overrunning guidance to about $17m; these sit below revenue and depress reported profit

quality.why: Headline revenue growth of 10.9% QoQ CC is driven by volume (eight large deals, order intake above $1bn, 3.8% organic sequential growth), but the brief shows Encore flat organically, so the rest of the headline growth reflects the acquisition consolidation rather than the recurring base; the brief does not quantify the acquired contribution precisely.
